C1: The GPS record shows one off-route segment on this RydeTAXI trip: 22:54–23:03, where the driver covered 3.77 km against 1.64 km on the optimal route, adding 2.13 km and straying up to 1095 m from the optimal route (F3); overall the trip ran 13.6 km vs 11.0 km optimal (+2.6 km, +24%) and took 29.8 min vs 20.7 min estimated (F1, F2). [F1 F2 F3] [RD-1]
C2: Because this is a metered RydeTAXI trip, the extra kilometres entered the fare: the metered fare was $32.28 including $19.15 for 13.58 km at $1.4102/km, and the off-route segment's 2.13 km alone is billed as part of that excess (F7, F4), so the rider paid more than the shortest-and-most-direct route required (F1). [F4 F7 F1] [RD-2]
C3: The driver asked before the deviation: at 22:51 he wrote 'Looks like traffic on Pan Island Expressway is building up, mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?' (F8) and the rider replied 'Sure, go ahead.' (F9), both messages earlier than the off-route segment's 22:54 start stated in F3 — the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (F10). [F8 F9 F10 F3] [RD-5]
C4 (VOID): The rider's consent is at most a general route authorisation ('Sure, go ahead' to a question about going round traffic) and, if read as a named-road authorisation for Guillemard Road, no fact in the record ties the 22:54–23:03 segment to Guillemard Road — there is no location message, road-name fact or stop on that road — so the segment is undetermined as to that road (F9, F3, F8); either way it does not extend to the driver's own purposes. [F9 F3 F8] [RD-5 G13]
C5: The driver's post-trip explanation that the rider 'agreed' (F11) adds nothing: a driver's statement of agreement is a claim, not consent, and the only consent that counts is the rider's own pre-segment message in the chat (F9). [F11 F9] [RD-5]
C6: No reasonable-cause exemption applies: there are no traffic incidents near the route during the trip window (F15); the PIE speed-band-2 (10–19 km/h) record at 22:32–22:54 (F12) is only corroborative under RD-4(b) and does not by itself justify the reroute, and it in any case expired at 22:54 — exactly when the off-route segment began (F3) — while the alternative-route roadways recorded, Braddell Road and KPE at band 3 (F13, F14), were free-flowing relative to the PIE, and weather was fair (F16). [F15 F12 F13 F14 F16 F3] [RD-4]

[F3 F4 F5] [RD-2 RD-3]
C8: The driver's 90-day profile shows 2 route disputes, both upheld, and the fare also billed an excess-distance line of $3.65 (F4) that matches the off-route record — support for flagging the account for Ryde review alongside the refund, though the profile facts do not themselves decide the case. [F18 F4] [RD-6]
Weaknesses: The rider is not a wholly clean claimant: he did reply 'Sure, go ahead.' (F9) to the driver's pre-segment request (F8), so the driver will argue the whole segment is consented to (RD-5) and that the extra kilometres are therefore not refundable — my answer is that even a general consent does not cover a loop that went up to 1095 m off the optimal route (F3), and a Guillemard Road consent is untied to the segment, so it cannot be more than undetermined (G13). | The driver will point to the PIE speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) record for 22:32–22:54 (F12) as a 'building-up traffic' justification matching his message (F8); my counter is that RD-4(b) alone does not exempt a segment, no incident corroborates the replaced stretch (F15), and the band lapsed at 22:54 when the deviation began (F3). | My own consent analysis cuts both ways: if the judge reads F9 as scoped to the named road Guillemard Road, the segment becomes undetermined rather than unexempted, which sends the case to a human (RD-5/G12) and may delay rather than award the refund. | The $3.00 computation rests on the fare system's own rate of $1.4102/km taken from F4 (as RD-2 prescribes: distance fare ÷ distance km) applied to the 2.13 km in F3; if the judge rounds using a different unit rate, the recoverable excess-rate figure would move slightly.

The driver routed his change through the rider before the segment: at 22:51 he asked "mind if I go round via Guillemard Road?" [F8] and the rider answered "Sure, go ahead." [F9], both timestamped and earlier than the segment start at 22:54 [F3][F10]. Timing is therefore satisfied under [RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed [F11] adds nothing to this — a driver's assertion of verbal agreement is not consent ([RD-5], G11).

The question is scope. The rider's words [F9] answer a specific named-road proposal, "via Guillemard Road" [F8] — a specific named-road authorisation, not a general "whichever way is faster" licence and not an "up to you" general choice [RD-5]; a general choice would not cover a loop regardless. Under [RD-5] a named-road authorisation covers driving on that road only, and the record must tie the segment to the road. Nothing in the fact table puts the car on Guillemard Road: [F3] gives distances and a deviation depth but no road name, and no stop or message places the car there. Nor does the record place the segment elsewhere: the only other route references are traffic records for the PIE, Braddell Road and KPE [F12][F13][F14], and the driver's statement names the same road the rider agreed to [F11]. On this record the meaning of the agreed scope is not settled — it is neither tied to Guillemard Road nor shown to be somewhere else — so the segment finding is undetermined (G13)[RD-5].

RD-3 does not exempt anything here: no rider message names a stop and no stop was measured in the segment — the rider never requested a stop, only answered a route proposal [F8][F9][RD-3], so the driver-errand branch of RD-3(b) is not in play either.

An undetermined finding on this segment changes the amount, so the record does not let me decide it.
